chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: What the draft and Army taught him
summary: He says being drafted was the best thing for him because he learned discipline and manhood.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And what was the next step for you?

Well, Charley's step led me right up into the war. I think that's the one mistake that Charley made. He was lucky enough for somebody to get him out of the draft. But that was the worst thing that ever happened to him. And it was the greatest thing that ever happened to me, that I didn't have sense enough to get out of the draft. Because, if I'd have could, no doubt I would have gotten out. As the guy said, "I fought and I fought, but they kept me anyhow." See?
But that's one thing was in my favor, that I didn't get out of it.
Now, how was that in your favor?

I learned how to deal with other people. I learnt how to obey the authorities, and how to respect those that are over you and how to know how to get out of those under you. Those are the things I learnt. I learnt manhood, I learnt to be a man and how to be a man. Which a lot of people don't know today.
